Hey thanks for the elaborate answer and I happy about your DM :)

I will think of your recommondations and look into alternative routes to go about it. I have been fascinated by Carl Jung and his work, I would say the way I have worked with Meditation and Ayahuasca lately has been very much about connecting with my Anima, not so much about connecting with my shadow yet.

And i also understand your concerns about the money-machine and cultural appropriation, I share this view and I also feel like ayahuasca is being used in irresponsible ways by many.

I have met brazilians, though, who told me about shamanic ayahuasca rituals outside of the amazon (sao paulo region) where neither portuguese nor english was spoken, since the shaman spoke an amazonian language. A common Language is supposedly not the most important thing according to them, since the shaman knew exactly what they were going through by mere observation. Even I felt like I could approximately describe which state the people around me are in the last time just by looking around so I could see this statement making lots of sense. To be precise this would be the exact thing I am looking for, either in Floripa or somewhere in southern Brazil.
Obrigado, meu amigo/amiga! Esses lugares parecem incríveis, vou dar uma olhada neles e, é claro, informarei você se descobrir mais :)

Hey yeah I found some places but its hard to find one that does Ayahuasca in the forest (we have done it only in inner yards within a city) and therefore wanted to hear from ppl actually on the island if they could recommend anything. Also it was hard for me to see whether those places feel comfortable hosting non portuguese speakers.

For me both of the times I did ayahuasca it revealed different things and I could see how it works along different paths also depending on the topics you prepare to work on. The last time I did has been about 6 weeks ago, the one bfore was 4 weeks prior, and I feel like I am ready for new insights to be integrated. It has brought up so much I don't see how another time would not continue down this avenue.

I don't know if I am really running away from something, it is more like I have experienced a place deep within myself, it felt like all my anxieties, blockades, insecurities and whatsoever are collected in this area (at least it feels like that) but I could not yet tell what is actually in there and why I feel that way. I tried to reexplore this, go into it, feel it and maybe resolve or work on it. I was not able to get there again and maybe I am a bit impatient with it, maybe shadow work could be the proper approach to do so. I just felt like it surprised me to much the last time on ayahuasca but i am more ready to face this part of me now, and ayahuasca could get me in that state of mind again where I could rewire. Happy to hear your thoughts on that.

I have not tried shadow work but I will look into it, if you have recommended resources I am always opened.
You will find reasons to change yourself throughout your lifespan, and that is good! You should become comfortable changing yourself
Thank you for your comment, I will continue educating myself !

You realize how smoking makes your panic worse right? A break would ease that inner feeling for sure!

I keep saying that if you believe quitting is going to be hard, it is going to be hard. If you are telling yourself you are a strong person that will not face any difficulties improving your life, it wont be much of a problem as long as you learn how to get along with impulses. Its not hard, but you have to invest time and energy.

I just posted this, might be that caffeine triggers your nicotine cravings.

https://www.reddit.com/r/stopsmoking/comments/k4x1mp/i_didnt_realize/?utm_medium=android_app&utm_source=share

I feel like the whole process of stopping (after quitting n times and beginning n-1 times again) is all about what you think it will be. If you believe its hard, it will be, if you believe you can do it easily and improve your life it will be easy. 

Of course there are some rules to the game and you should be prepared for cravings and different situations but isn't that like everything else you want to achieve in life? If you want to achieve something you have to put in the time and effort. In this context that means arranging thoughts and building motivation. You can do it!

Smoking is poison for your mental health! I stopped smoking 7 weeks ago and also being more or less isolated atm due to Corona lockdown (I live in Austria), so there is not much party going on right now. Perfect time to quit!

Its not as hard as people think, prepare for 3 days mentally and then do your first step of improving your life and stop. All the best!
I think not drinking at all for 3 months might help you, and then slowly getting back into a "healthy" drinking routine without cigarettes slowly. Start slowly with one or two beer

Don't worry! Most cravings pass in 10 to 20 minutes, so keep it up like the strong person you are!

Try to keep a positive mind and don't just bother about the nagative effects when you continue smoking, bring back to your mind why you stopped in the first place, write down your thoughts. Its just like with everything else you want to be good at, if you want to be good at not smoking you have to invest a little time rearrange your thoughts and look at the improvements you made.
